editorial:
Imagine being a teacher who thinks school rumors are just kids being kids, only to find out a viral video is actually killing your students. That is exactly what happens to Akane. You will feel her panic as she realizes a creepy man named Kashiwada is using the internet to spread a deadly curse. The vibe here is very tense and modern, mixing the old-school creepiness of Sadako with today's digital world. You get to follow Akane and her boyfriend Takanori as they try to stop a madman who wants to bring back a ghost to cause total chaos.

What really pops in this one are the jump scares and the way the movie plays with your eyes. The acting is solid, and the pacing keeps you on your toes without feeling too slow. While some of the plot points are a bit wild, it is a fun ride if you love J-horror. You should definitely try streaming this in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to get the best picture quality, or just rent it on Apple TV for a movie night. It is a great pick for a rainy weekend with friends.
endingExplained: In the final act, you see that Kashiwada wants to use the 3D technology to bring Sadako into the real world. He thinks he can control her, but he is wrong. Sadako eventually takes over and attacks everyone. Akane and Takanori fight back to stop the cycle of death. In the end, they manage to defeat the villain and stop the curse from spreading further, though the scare of Sadako remains.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves creepy ghost stories and Japanese horror movies.
